subject: Post-call recap: Redwood inference pilot & procurement path
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Chen <dchen@optimahealth.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@optimahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood inference pilot & procurement path

Hi Daniel / Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment with the executive sponsors and procurement path.

Key pain points we heard
- Latency spikes on current vendor during peak clinical workloads (p95 ~ 800ms) impacting patient-facing features.
- Unpredictable per-token spend — finance wants a clearer unit cost and enrollment/commit options.
- Data residency & PHI concerns — security needs SOC 2 and KMS controls documented.

Business goals / success metrics
- Reduce inference p95 latency to <200ms for 95% of requests for the triage microservice.
- Achieve ~50–75% cost reduction on serving costs vs current vendor through batching and quantization recommendations.
- Complete a 6-week pilot with measurable latency/cost dashboards and an evaluation report for execs.

Procurement & timeline notes
- Sarah (CISO) will run a security review —she asked for SOC 2 summary and architecture diagram.
- Procurement team indicated they want a standard PO path if SLA/terms are acceptable; tentative target to finalize PO by end of May.
- Executive sponsors: Daniel (VP Eng) + Sarah (CISO).

Escalation / risks called out on the call
- Need SOC 2 summary and data flow diagram within 3 business days to stay on the proposed timeline.
- If private deployment is required, procurement will need an onboarding estimate & pricing for Dedicated capacity.

Attachments I'm sharing
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 control mapping + attestation stub)
- optima-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP with milestones & owners)

Proposed next steps
1) I will send the SOC 2 summary + short architecture note today (attached).
2) Daniel / Sarah: confirm pilot scope (six-week pilot, triage microservice, target dataset) by EOD Wed 3/18.
3) I'll schedule a brief procurement/finance sync week of 3/22 to review PO path and pricing options (commit vs pay-as-you-go).

If it helps, we can offer a pilot credit and an SLA addendum for the pilot period —happy to have Laura (my manager) join that conversation.

Thanks — look forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, optima-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood inference pilot & procurement path

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming executive sponsors: yes, I'm sponsoring the pilot from Eng and Sarah will lead the security review.
- Timeline: security review kickoff ASAP; procurement's internal target is to have a PO ready by Friday, 29 May, assuming no major redlines. I'll sync with procurement and share a point of contact (they're copied).
- Pilot scope: triage microservice is correct — we want you to run against our anonymized recent workload and provide the latency/cost dashboard. We will share a small subset of production traces for validation.

Action items on my side:
- Sarah: lead security review and share any additional requirements to Marissa.
- Procurement: I'll push to get a single PO owner and timeline — will follow up with a contact this week.

One ask: if you can confirm whether a private Dedicated deployment is required to meet PHI constraints or whether hosted with VPC/KMS will suffice, that will shape the procurement path.

Appreciate the offer of pilot credits — that will help expedite legal approvals.

Regards,
Daniel Chen
VP Engineering, Optima Health

Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: Redwood inference pilot & procurement path — exec recap for leadership

Laura / Rishi —

Executive summary for leadership and required escalation items based on yesterday's call with Optima Health. Putting this in writing so we're aligned before we loop legal/procurement.

Business outcomes they need
- Clear SLAs on p95 latency for the triage microservice (target <200ms). Success of pilot judged on latency improvements + cost delta.
- Decision point at end of pilot: move to Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted with replication in us-east and VPC/KMS.

Risk & compliance
- PHI considerations: Sarah (CISO) requires SOC 2 evidence and a data flow diagram. If we cannot demonstrate hosted VPC/KMS meets their PHI needs, they will require Private/Dedicated deployment which increases onboarding time and cost.

Procurement path / timeline
- Procurement has a target PO date of 2026-05-29, contingent on security and legal reviews.
- We should prepare two pricing pathways: (A) 6-week pilot on hosted (with pilot credits + SLA addendum) and (B) dedicated deployment estimate + onboarding timeline.

Escalation items (asks of Redwood leadership)
1) Approve offering pilot credit (up to $25k served as credits) and an SLA addendum for the pilot window to reduce procurement friction.
2) Prioritize SOC 2 summary + architecture note turnaround (within 3 business days). I attached the SOC 2 doc already sent to Optima.
3) If Optima requires Dedicated, we need a fast-track onboarding estimate (2–3 weeks) and a committed engineer for the ramp.

Next steps I'm taking
- Send SOC 2 summary and a short architecture note today (done).
- Draft MAP milestones and owners in the attached XLSX and share for comment by Wed 3/18.
- Coordinate procurement touchpoint for week of 3/22.

If approved, we should communicate the pilot credit and fast-track option to procurement as a way to keep the deal on the May timeline.

Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
